item.title: Cell biologists uncover key mechanism behind a rare cause of childhood epilepsy
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

University of Liverpool scientists found how CDKL5 protein, linked to severe childhood epilepsy, is positioned in nerve cells. CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD) affects 1 in 40,000-60,000 births. The study reveals a new molecular docking mechanism at synapses, showing CDKL5's location is crucial for normal brain function. The research suggests some mutations may disrupt CDKL5 positioning, affecting neurological development.

Source: Medical Xpress | Published: 2026-11-20 19:00 UTC

Original link: https://medicalxpress.com/news/2026-11-cell-biologists-uncover-key-mechanism.html

item.title: Inner ear study challenges canonical understanding of hearing
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

New research challenges the traditional 'place code' model of hearing, suggesting a more complex processing of low frequencies in the inner ear. This could improve cochlear implant technology. The study, using optical coherence tomography, found low frequencies cause synchronized responses across the cochlea, contradicting the simple frequency-to-place mapping. The research, published in Science Advances, could lead to better hearing technology and a deeper understanding of hearing.

Source: Medical Xpress | Published: 2026-11-20 19:00 UTC

Original link: https://medicalxpress.com/news/2026-11-ear-canonical.html

item.title: Patients have little say in how brain implant trials are done. Ian Burkhart wants to change that
item.description:

Patients in brain implant trials often have limited influence over research and data privacy. The BCI Pioneers Coalition report suggests 13 recommendations for better post-trial care, informed consent, and neural data privacy. Ian Burkhart, co-founder of the coalition, emphasizes the need for more participant agency and long-term care support for BCI users.

item.title: Opinion: More doctors should prescribe exercise after a concussion
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Two decades ago, a Vespa accident left me with a coma and post-concussion symptoms. Exercise, including yoga and skate skiing, helped my recovery. New research suggests exercise aids concussion recovery, though more studies are needed. Currently, exercise is rarely prescribed for brain injuries, despite its potential benefits.
